papers.title: The Utility of Abstaining in Binary Classification
papers.abstract: We explore the problem of binary classification in machine learning, with a twist - the classifier is allowed to abstain on any datum, professing ignorance about the true class label without committing to any prediction. This is directly motivated by applications like medical diagnosis and fraud risk assessment, in which incorrect predictions have potentially calamitous consequences. We focus on a recent spate of theoretically driven work in this area that characterizes how allowing abstentions can lead to fewer errors in very general settings. Two areas are highlighted: the surprising possibility of zero-error learning, and the fundamental tradeoff between predicting sufficiently often and avoiding incorrect predictions. We review efficient algorithms with provable guarantees for each of these areas. We also discuss connections to other scenarios, notably active learning, as they suggest promising directions of further inquiry in this emerging field.

summary_en.motivation: To reduce catastrophic errors in high-stakes binary classification by allowing abstention.
summary_en.method: Surveys theoretical results and efficient algorithms for classification with abstention.
summary_en.result: Demonstrates the possibility of zero-error learning and the tradeoff between prediction frequency and accuracy.
summary_en.validation: Purely theoretical analysis without experimental validation.

papers.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Deep Gaussian Process
papers.abstract: We propose a new approach to inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) based on the deep Gaussian process (deep GP) model, which is capable of learning complicated reward structures with few demonstrations. Our model stacks multiple latent GP layers to learn abstract representations of the state feature space, which is linked to the demonstrations through the Maximum Entropy learning framework. Incorporating the IRL engine into the nonlinear latent structure renders existing deep GP inference approaches intractable. To tackle this, we develop a non-standard variational approximation framework which extends previous inference schemes. This allows for approximate Bayesian treatment of the feature space and guards against overfitting. Carrying out representation and inverse reinforcement learning simultaneously within our model outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, as we demonstrate with experiments on standard benchmarks ("object world","highway driving") and a new benchmark ("binary world").

summary_en.motivation: To learn complex reward functions from few demonstrations using a flexible Bayesian nonparametric model.
summary_en.method: Combine deep Gaussian processes with maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning, employing a novel variational inference framework.
summary_en.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art IRL methods on standard and new benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Validated on simulated environments ('object world', 'highway driving', 'binary world').
